text:
**Score:** 5/10

The code is reasonably organized and has useful unit tests, but I would not approve it as-is. The biggest blockers are that a fresh `make demo` cannot actually bootstrap its required story data, story generation depends on a manifest that may not exist yet, default tests do not exercise the real pipeline, and generated artifacts/package metadata are committed into the repo.

I estimate about **260 lines** need rewriting or significant changes, plus removal of generated artifacts. That includes CLI/data bootstrapping, artifact hygiene, dependency/test setup, numerical edge cases, and added regression tests.

Verification: `pytest -q` could not collect because this environment lacks dependencies like `numpy`; AST parsing of all Python files passed.

issues.description: Default pipeline points at data/stories, but the repo has no story dataset, so make demo/all cannot run from a fresh checkout.
generate-stories tries to load data/stories/manifest.json before generating stories, making first-time dataset generation impossible without a preexisting manifest.
Story response parsing treats any preamble before the first <NEW STORY> marker as a story, which can silently corrupt generated datasets.
HTTP story generation has no timeout, so a hung API endpoint can block the command indefinitely.
PCA component selection divides by total variance without handling zero-variance inputs, producing NaNs on degenerate activation data.
mean_activations can divide by zero for one-token encoded inputs because effective_start may equal the sequence length.
load_vectors trusts saved artifacts without validating model name, layer count, dimensions, or emotion compatibility against the active run.
Core ML dependencies are unbounded lower-only ranges, which leaves the project exposed to breaking upstream changes.
The only end-to-end pipeline test is excluded by default, so normal test runs do not verify extraction, validation, or steering behavior.
Importing the package mutates process-wide environment variables, which is surprising global side effect for a library import.
Generated egg-info metadata is committed, which is stale build output and should not live in source control.
Generated binary experiment artifacts are committed under outputs, adding repository noise and reproducibility ambiguity.
